alolan.label: Alolan form
alolan.text: Pokémon that adapted to the tropical islands of Alola. Regional forms began here, in Pokémon Sun and Moon (Generation 7).

baby.label: Baby Pokémon
baby.text: The first stage of a family, which can't breed itself though its evolved forms can. Babies arrived in Generation 2, along with breeding.

branch.label: Branched evolution
branch.text: A Pokémon that can evolve into more than one species. What decides the branch differs from family to family: an item, a time of day, a stat, or something hidden.

form_change.label: Form change
form_change.text: A switch between looks that isn't evolution: the Pokémon can change back, and it stays the same species.

fusion.label: Fusion
fusion.text: A legendary Pokémon joining with another into one, using a special item, and splitting apart again later: Kyurem with Zekrom or Reshiram, Necrozma with Solgaleo or Lunala, Calyrex with Glastrier or Spectrier.

galarian.label: Galarian form
galarian.text: Pokémon that adapted to the Galar region of Pokémon Sword and Shield (Generation 8). Some Galarian forms evolve into species found nowhere else, like Perrserker.

gigantamax.label: Gigantamax
gigantamax.text: A special kind of Dynamax from Pokémon Sword and Shield that makes a Pokémon enormous and changes how it looks. Only Pokémon with the Gigantamax Factor can do it, and only for a short time.

hisuian.label: Hisuian form
hisuian.text: Pokémon of Hisui, the region that would become Sinnoh, as they lived long ago in Pokémon Legends: Arceus (Generation 8). Some Hisuian forms evolve into species found nowhere else, like Sneasler and Overqwil.

kantonian.label: Kantonian
kantonian.text: The original look of a species that also has regional forms, named after Kanto, where it was first found. Games just call it Meowth; the adjective is used when the forms need telling apart.

mega.label: Mega Evolution
mega.text: A transformation in battle, introduced in Pokémon X and Y: the Pokémon holds its Mega Stone and its Trainer activates a Key Stone. It lasts for that battle only.

paldean.label: Paldean form
paldean.text: Pokémon that adapted to the Paldea region of Pokémon Scarlet and Violet (Generation 9), like Paldean Wooper and the three breeds of Paldean Tauros.

primal.label: Primal Reversion
primal.text: A return to an ancient, more powerful form, from Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire: Kyogre does it holding the Blue Orb, Groudon holding the Red Orb. Like Mega Evolution, it lasts for one battle.

regional.label: Regional form
regional.text: The same species adapted to a different region's habitat, often with a new look and a new type. Four regions have them so far: Alola, Galar, Hisui and Paldea.

regional_evolution.label: Regional evolution
regional_evolution.text: A new species that only a regional form evolves into. Galarian Meowth becomes Perrserker; Meowth from anywhere else still becomes Persian.

regional_rule.label: Evolving into a regional form
regional_rule.text: When a Pokémon evolves into a species that has a regional form, it takes the form of the region it is in, wherever it came from. A Pikachu given a Thunder Stone in Alola becomes Alolan Raichu.
